description: Which app icon matches each built-in Control UI theme. This file is the ONE owner: core/app-icons.js reads it on the desktop, the iOS app bundles it (mobile/Chela/AppIcons.swift), and desktop/scripts/artwork.mjs draws each theme's neon (dark) and paper (light) icon from its dark accent.
why: A theme is recognised by its accent, not its name. Neither client can read the theme's name, only the computed values it resolves to, and every built-in theme has a distinct accent in each mode. Both accents are listed so a theme is recognised whichever mode it is in.

The accents are copied from the Control UI's own theme files (ui/public/themes/*.css, and ui/src/styles/base.css for Claw). core/test/app-icons.test.js holds them to that checkout when one is present, the same arrangement as upstream-reference.json.
Claw is the primary icon because it is the default theme. A theme that is not listed, meaning a custom one, gets the primary icon too, since no icon can ship for a palette nobody has chosen yet.
